Tabletop Game Scale Guide

Every tabletop game scales its minis differently, and figuring out the right slicer percentage for your army should not take hours of searching. Pick a game below to open its full 3D-printing scale guide — the exact slicer percentage, printing settings, and conversion data for scaling those STL files on your FDM printer.

6mm Scale

1 system

Mech Tactical Wargame (6mm / 1:285)

Independent publisher
1:285

A tactical wargame where players control giant robotic war machines called battle mechs. Miniatures are 6mm scale (approximately 1:285), with 'mechs ranging from 30mm to 55mm tall depending on weight class. The game uses hex-movement rather than measuring tapes.

Sci-fi Tactical Wargame · 6mm

Epic-Scale Sci-Fi (8mm)

Independent publisher
1:200

This is the modern return to epic-scale sci-fi warfare, covering a galaxy-spanning civil war with hundreds of miniatures on a single table. At 8mm, individual soldiers are tiny but recognizable, and towering walkers loom over entire formations.

Epic-Scale Sci-fi Wargame · 8mm

10mm Scale

Sci-Fi Mass Battle (10mm / 1:160)

Independent publisher
1:160

A 10mm sci-fi wargame depicting massive far-future battles with infantry, tanks, and dropships. The small scale allows entire companies with transport vehicles to be fielded in a single game, emphasizing combined-arms tactics over individual heroics.

15mm Scale

1 system

WWII Company Wargame (15mm / 1:100)

Independent publisher
1:100

One of the most widely played 15mm WWII wargames, covering company-level engagements across all major theaters. Miniatures are 1:100 scale, allowing entire companies with supporting armor to fit on a standard gaming table. A companion Cold War-era variant extends the system to modern armor conflicts.

Classic Ranked Fantasy (28mm)

Independent publisher
1:56

A revival of the classic ranked fantasy style — regiment blocks, tile-based movement, and a hand-painted campaign map. It uses the legacy 28mm fantasy scale, making it compatible with decades of classic miniatures alongside new releases.

Fantasy Skirmish (25–28mm)

Independent publisher
1:56

A skirmish-focused wargame set in a beloved mythic fantasy world where individual heroes matter as much as armies. The range spans from 25mm (older metal sculpts from the early 2000s) to modern 28mm plastic kits.

Fantasy Skirmish Wargame · 28mm

WWII Platoon Wargame (28mm True Scale)

Independent publisher
1:56

One of the most widely played WWII tabletop wargames, covering platoon-level engagements from 1939-1945. Infantry are 28mm true scale (1:56), and vehicle kits from several manufacturers follow the same ratio, making 1:35 model kit vehicles usable after slight downsizing.

Historical Wargame (WWII) · 28mm

Classic Fantasy RPG (28mm)

Independent publisher
1:56

The original tabletop roleplaying game — players create characters and go on collaborative storytelling adventures. Miniatures are optional but widely used for combat encounters, with a Medium creature (human-sized) typically measuring 28mm to eye level on a 175cm baseline.

1:56

A Japanese-anime-influenced sci-fi skirmish game set in a far-future human sphere. The publisher's metal miniatures are renowned for their dynamic poses and intricate detail, with slimmer proportions than heroic-scale games despite the 28mm designation.

Independent publisher

32mm Scale

Sci-Fi Epic Wargame (Heroic 32mm)

Independent publisher
1:50

The biggest sci-fi tabletop wargame out there — power-armoured soldiers, alien hordes, chaos cults, and dozens of other factions fighting it out in a far-future galaxy. Modern kits since the 2017 range refresh sit squarely at 32mm heroic scale, while older classic models measure closer to 28mm true scale.

Sci-fi Wargame · 32mm
4 conversions

Modern Fantasy Wargame (Heroic 32mm)

Independent publisher
1:50

This modern fantasy wargame replaced ranked infantry blocks with hero-focused skirmish and mass battle in a high-fantasy setting. The miniature scale matches the modern sci-fi standard — all current fantasy releases since 2015 are 32mm heroic.

Fantasy Wargame · 32mm

1:50

A card-driven skirmish game set in a gothic steampunk alternate Earth where magic and technology collide. Miniatures are 32mm heroic scale, molded in high-quality plastic with a distinctive artistic style that blends horror, western, and Victorian aesthetics.

A specialist-led sci-fi skirmish game set in the same far-future universe as the 32mm epic standard. Instead of massive army battles, you field a small squad of specialists — a sniper, a medic, a heavy weapons trooper — each with unique abilities. Sci-Fi Mass Battle (35mm Eye Level)

Independent publisher
1:47

A rank-and-file mass battle game set in a beloved space opera universe, covering the classic film era and beyond. Miniatures are measured at 35mm eye level (1:47 scale), making them noticeably larger than the 32mm standard but smaller than 40mm skirmish games.

Superhero Skirmish (35mm True Scale)

Independent publisher
1:48

A cinematic skirmish game pitting comic-book superheroes and villains against each other in tabletop battles. The game uses 35mm true scale with realistic proportions — no heroic exaggeration — making the miniatures notably larger and more detailed than standard 32mm equivalents.

Fantasy Mass Battle (35mm)

Independent publisher
1:48

A mass-battle fantasy wargame with a unique alternating activation system that keeps both players engaged throughout the game. The setting features a dozen factions in a grim, low-fantasy world. The game uses 35mm scale, making it slightly larger than the 32mm standard and closer to 35mm mass-battle baselines.

Sci-Fi Dogfight (1:27)

Independent publisher
1:27

A miniatures game of space combat where players pilot iconic starfighters and freighters in fast-paced dogfights. The game uses pre-painted plastic ships at 1:27 ratio scale, covering everything from tiny interceptors to enormous transports. There are no infantry-scale miniatures — every model is a vehicle or ship.

Vehicular Combat (1:56)

A post-apocalyptic vehicular combat game that uses modified die-cast toy cars as miniatures. At 1:56 scale, these toy cars are compatible with 28mm infantry, making it easy to add foot soldiers, terrain, and custom 3D printed accessories.
